subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the reaction N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3, how many moles of NH3 form from 6 mol of H2 (excess N2)?
questions.explain: From the 3:2 ratio, 6 mol H2 produces (2/3) × 6 = 4 mol NH3.

questions.q: A gas occupies 2.40 dm3 at 100 kPa and 300 K. Using pV = nRT (R = 8.31), how many moles are present?
A compound has empirical formula CH2 and Mr = 56. What is its molecular formula? (Ar: C=12, H=1)
questions.explain: Empirical mass = 14; 56/14 = 4, so the molecular formula is C4H8.

questions.q: Which expression correctly gives the number of moles from a titration volume V (cm3) and concentration c (mol/dm3)?
questions.explain: Moles = concentration × volume in dm3 = c × V/1000 when V is in cm3.

questions.q: In chromatography, separation occurs because components have different:
options: Affinities for (distributions between) the stationary and mobile phases
questions.explain: Components separate according to how strongly they are retained by the stationary phase relative to the moving mobile phase.

questions.q: Adding D2O to an NMR sample causes a signal from an O-H or N-H proton to:
options: Disappear, because the labile proton is exchanged for deuterium
questions.explain: Labile O-H and N-H protons exchange with deuterium from D2O, so their signal disappears, helping identify them.

questions.q: What does the integration (relative area under each peak) in a 1H NMR spectrum tell you?
options: The ratio of the numbers of protons in each environment
questions.explain: The integration trace gives the relative number of hydrogen atoms responsible for each signal.

questions.q: What is the Mr of CuSO4·5H2O? (Ar: Cu=63.5, S=32, O=16, H=1)
In the mass spectrum of a compound, a fragment at m/z 29 lost from the molecular ion most likely corresponds to:
questions.explain: A peak at m/z 29 commonly corresponds to CHO+ or C2H5+, a characteristic fragment.

questions.q: How many moles of oxygen atoms are in 0.5 mol of Al2(SO4)3?
questions.explain: Each formula unit contains 12 oxygen atoms, so 0.5 × 12 = 6 mol of oxygen atoms.

questions.q: What mass of CaCO3 (Mr = 100) is needed to provide 0.25 mol?
questions.explain: Mass = moles × Mr = 0.25 × 100 = 25 g.

questions.q: How many peaks (signals) are seen in the 13C NMR spectrum of benzene, C6H6?
questions.explain: All six carbon atoms in benzene are equivalent by symmetry, so only one 13C signal is observed.

questions.q: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 8.0 g but only 6.0 g is obtained. What is the percentage yield?
questions.explain: Percentage yield = (actual/theoretical) × 100 = (6.0/8.0) × 100 = 75%.

questions.q: To deduce a full structure, chemists combine techniques: mass spectrometry gives Mr, IR gives functional groups, and NMR gives:
questions.explain: NMR reveals the number of carbon and hydrogen environments plus splitting/integration, establishing how atoms are connected.

questions.q: In 1H NMR, the number of separate signals (peaks) corresponds to:
options: The number of different proton (hydrogen) environments
The total number of hydrogen atoms
questions.explain: Each set of chemically equivalent protons gives one signal, so the number of signals equals the number of proton environments.

questions.q: At 273 K and 101 kPa, what volume does 0.5 mol of ideal gas occupy? (Molar gas volume ≈ 22.4 dm3 at stp)
questions.explain: Volume = 0.5 × 22.4 = 11.2 dm3 at standard temperature and pressure.

questions.q: In CaCO3 → CaO + CO2, what mass of CaO (Mr=56) forms from 10 g of CaCO3 (Mr=100)?
questions.explain: Moles CaCO3 = 10/100 = 0.10; this gives 0.10 mol CaO; mass = 0.10 × 56 = 5.6 g.

questions.q: What is the molar mass of a gas if 0.50 g occupies 0.40 dm3 at stp (molar volume 22.4 dm3/mol)?
How many moles are present in 12 g of carbon-12? (Ar = 12)
questions.explain: Moles = mass/Mr = 12/12 = 1 mol.

questions.q: What is the atom economy for producing H2 in the reaction Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2? (Mr: H2=2, ZnCl2=136)
questions.explain: Atom economy = (Mr desired/total Mr of products) × 100 = (2/138) × 100 ≈ 1.4%.

questions.q: How many grams of water are lost when 0.10 mol of MgSO4·7H2O is fully dehydrated? (Mr H2O = 18)
questions.explain: Each mole contains 7 mol water; 0.10 × 7 × 18 = 12.6 g of water lost.

questions.q: How many proton (1H) environments are present in 1,4-dimethylbenzene (para-xylene)?
questions.explain: Symmetry makes the two CH3 groups equivalent and the four aromatic H equivalent, giving 2 proton environments.

questions.q: 25.0 cm3 of a NaOH solution requires 22.5 cm3 of 0.100 mol/dm3 HCl for neutralisation (1:1). What is the NaOH concentration?
questions.explain: Moles HCl = 0.100 × 22.5/1000 = 0.00225 mol = moles NaOH; concentration = 0.00225/0.0250 = 0.0900 mol/dm3.

questions.q: What is the empirical formula of a compound containing 40% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O by mass? (Ar: C=12, H=1, O=16)
questions.explain: Dividing by Ar gives ratios 3.33 : 6.7 : 3.33 = 1 : 2 : 1, so the empirical formula is CH2O.

questions.q: How many moles of HCl are in 50.0 cm3 of 0.200 mol/dm3 solution?
What is the concentration of a solution made by dissolving 0.5 mol of NaCl in water to give 250 cm3 of solution?
questions.explain: Concentration = moles/volume = 0.5 / 0.250 = 2 mol/dm3.

questions.q: A compound shows molecular ion peaks at m/z 78 and 80 in a 3:1 ratio. This indicates the presence of:
questions.explain: The 3:1 ratio of M to M+2 reflects the 75.5:24.5 abundance of 35Cl to 37Cl, indicating one chlorine atom.

questions.q: Why is tetramethylsilane (TMS) used as the reference standard in NMR?
options: It gives a single sharp peak defined as 0 ppm and is inert and volatile
It absorbs strongly in the IR
questions.explain: TMS has 12 equivalent protons giving one sharp signal set as 0 ppm; it is inert and easily removed by evaporation.

questions.q: In the reaction 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO, which is the limiting reagent if 0.10 mol Mg reacts with 0.10 mol O2?
questions.explain: The 2:1 ratio means 0.10 mol Mg needs only 0.05 mol O2; Mg runs out first so it is limiting.

questions.q: In the mass spectrum of propanone (CH3COCH3), a strong fragment at m/z 43 is due to:
questions.explain: Propanone fragments by losing a methyl group to give the stable acylium ion CH3CO+ at m/z 43.
